headline: ASX dips slightly as the RBA rate-cut dream fades further, while gold hits record highs and your US stocks had a mixed night.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two had a solid session last night, up 1.87% to $254.99 USD. No specific news catalyst, but the stock has been riding broader gaming sector momentum. You're now sitting on a healthy +11.18% gain overall on this one.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft jumped 1.62% last night to $390.49 USD, driven by news it's launching a $2.5 billion 'Frontier Company' focused on enterprise AI — basically a new business unit to sell AI tools to large corporations. The market liked the aggressive AI push. You're still down about 11.87% overall on this position though, so it's working its way back.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: FUEL closed up 1.3% today to $7.77 AUD. Energy ETFs got a lift as analysts flagged ASX energy shares as back in focus despite slightly softer crude oil prices. Traders appear to be rotating back into the sector on value grounds.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS was today's biggest loser in your portfolio, dropping 1.72% to $5.14 AUD. Lithium stocks remain under pressure as the sector waits for a clear price recovery — reports today noted that 'price recovery discipline' is the key watch for lithium miners right now. You're down 23.74% overall on this one, which remains the portfolio's biggest drag.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE edged up 0.6% today to $95.67 AUD, a quiet positive session with no specific news. Emerging markets broadly steady.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI crept up 0.12% today to $16.76 AUD. The AI ETF space is getting attention as semiconductor stocks come back into focus, but the move today was minimal. Still down 11.26% overall from your entry price.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG barely moved today, up just 0.09% to $76.28 AUD. A flat session for the broad diversified ETF, which is exactly what you'd expect on a quiet day. Vanguard's ETFs overall had a strong FY26, with the latest data showing record ETF listings on the ASX.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS was essentially flat today at $533.31 AUD, up just 0.05 cents. The US market ETF barely budged as it digests last night's mixed US session — the NASDAQ fell 0.8% but the S&P 500 was dead flat.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google slipped 0.48% last night to $356.18 USD with no specific news attached — just a soft NASDAQ session overall where tech gave back some ground. You're still up 15.85% overall on this position, one of the best performers in the portfolio.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Lithium pain continues
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals dropped another 1.72% today and you're now down nearly 24% on this position. Multiple analyst pieces today flagged that lithium's recovery depends on 'price discipline' from miners — there's no clear catalyst for a bounce yet. Worth reviewing whether you want to hold through a potentially long bottoming process.

watch_today.title: MSFT — AI momentum building
watch_today.detail: Microsoft's $2.5 billion new enterprise AI business unit announcement helped push the stock up 1.62% last night. The company is clearly doubling down on AI as its core growth story. You're still 11.87% underwater overall, but this is a meaningful step toward recovery. Hold and watch.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI ETF still underwater, but sector tailwinds building
watch_today.detail: GXAI crept up 0.12% today but remains 11.26% below your entry. Semiconductor stocks are back in focus and AI regulation headlines (see AI section) are keeping the theme top of mind globally. No reason to sell here — the long-term thesis is intact, you're just waiting for the market to catch up.

watch_today.title: No RBA rate cuts until 2027 — what it means for your portfolio
watch_today.detail: Multiple economists today said rate cuts are all but ruled out until 2027, with a fourth rate rise still possible. This is a headwind for ASX growth stocks and property-linked assets, and means Aussie consumer spending stays under pressure. Your diversified ETFs (VDHG, VTS) are relatively insulated, but keep it in mind for any new ASX positions.

watch_today.title: Gold surging — worth knowing
watch_today.detail: Gold jumped 1.34% last night to $4,167 USD per ounce — that's a significant move. None of your holdings are directly exposed to gold, but it signals investors are nervous and seeking safe havens. Keep an eye on whether this flight-to-safety mood starts dragging on your growth/tech holdings.

watch_today.title: TTWO — riding momentum
watch_today.detail: Take-Two is up 1.87% last night and now 11.18% above your entry price — the best performing US holding by total return. No specific news, just solid momentum. Happy to keep riding this one.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 dipped 0.15% today to close at 8,831 — a quiet session with no major drama. Last night on Wall Street, the S&P 500 was dead flat (basically unchanged) while the NASDAQ fell 0.8%, dragged down by tech stocks giving back recent gains. The big story in markets right now is gold, which shot up 1.34% to over $4,167 USD an ounce — investors are clearly looking for safety. The Aussie dollar nudged up slightly to 69.3 US cents, and oil was marginally softer at $68.53 a barrel.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Tech gave back ground last night

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is that rate cut hopes have been crushed — economists are now saying the RBA won't cut until 2027 at the earliest, and another rate rise is still on the table. On top of that, Australia has just been ranked as having the worst inflation among all major developed economies. Not great reading for mortgage holders.

stories.title: Rate cuts ruled out until 2027 — and a fourth hike is still possible
stories.why_it_matters: Multiple economists have now told the AFR and Nine that the Reserve Bank is unlikely to cut interest rates before 2027, with some saying a fourth rate rise is still on the cards if inflation stays stubborn. This means mortgage repayments stay high for longer — bad news for households already stretched thin. For investors, it keeps pressure on the ASX and makes fixed-rate and defensive assets more attractive relative to growth stocks.

stories.title: Australia tops inflation rankings among all major developed economies
stories.why_it_matters: A new ranking published by the AFR shows Australia now has the highest inflation rate among all major developed economies — worse than the US, UK, Europe and Japan. This helps explain why the RBA is so reluctant to cut rates. For everyday Aussies, it means the cost of living squeeze is likely to continue well into next year, and it puts pressure on the Albanese government heading toward the next election cycle.

ai.summary: Today's AI news was dominated by one big theme: governments around the world are scrambling to regulate AI before it gets away from them. From the UN to Spain to Europe, everyone is trying to figure out the rules — and they're all running behind the technology. There's also a practical consumer angle with a deal on AI subscriptions.

stories.title: UN chief issues urgent call for AI and 'killer robot' governance
stories.why_it_matters: UN Secretary-General António Guterres has made an urgent call for international rules governing both AI systems and autonomous weapons (so-called 'killer robots' — drones and military systems that can make lethal decisions without a human in the loop). The concern is that technology is outpacing any meaningful international framework, and without rules, there's no floor on how these tools get used in conflict. For AI investors, more global governance pressure could mean compliance costs for the big tech players — but it could also mean more regulated, stable markets long-term.

stories.title: Spain pushes for AI regulation to protect workers
stories.why_it_matters: Spain is pushing hard within the EU for AI rules specifically designed to protect workers — particularly around AI being used to monitor employees, make hiring/firing decisions, or automate jobs without human oversight. This is one of the more concrete proposals coming out of Europe right now. For companies like Google and Microsoft (both in your portfolio) that sell AI workplace tools, European labour regulations could add compliance costs or limit how aggressively they can deploy AI products in that market.

stories.title: Is AI developing faster than governments can regulate it?
stories.why_it_matters: A growing body of analysis today flagged that AI capabilities — particularly in areas like autonomous agents, multimodal models (systems that can see, hear, and talk, not just read text), and self-improving systems — are advancing much faster than any government's ability to write meaningful rules. The concern isn't just theoretical: real decisions about employment, healthcare, and finance are already being made by AI systems that have no legal accountability framework around them. Worth watching as a long-term risk for the sector.

stories.title: Get ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude for life for $70 — today only
stories.why_it_matters: A one-day deal is offering lifetime access to ChatGPT (OpenAI), Gemini (Google) and Claude (Anthropic) — three of the world's leading AI assistants — bundled together for $70 USD. If you're not already using these tools, this is a cheap way to get access to all three and see which suits your workflow. Worth grabbing if you want to experiment with AI in everyday tasks like research, writing, or financial planning.

sport.summary: The Knights knocked off the Dolphins last weekend to end their win streak, the NRL is making a play for Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce, Wimbledon is well underway with Naomi Osaka turning heads, and there's a big AFL Thursday night clash coming up.

stories.title: Knights end Dolphins' win streak in a thriller — and NRL wants Swift and Kelce courtside
stories.why_it_matters: The Newcastle Knights beat the Dolphins in a tight one on the weekend, ending Redcliffe's win streak. Fox Sports praised 'Brown brilliance' as a decisive factor. In a separate story, the NRL is reportedly trying to lure Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce to a game — a Hail Mary PR move following the Knights result that ended the Dolphins' momentum.

stories.title: Manly cops top-four reality check as Eels veteran stuns with highlight reel moment
stories.why_it_matters: Manly Sea Eagles got a reality check on their top-four aspirations over the weekend, with the Parramatta Eels pulling off a standout result. A veteran Eels player produced a 'highlight reel' moment that Fox Sports flagged as one of the plays of the round. Manly host the Cowboys in Round 19 on Sunday — a must-watch given the ladder implications.

stories.title: Naomi Osaka surging at Wimbledon — Sabalenka knocked out
stories.why_it_matters: Naomi Osaka is making serious noise at Wimbledon 2026, with the SMH describing her as a genuine title contender after her brilliant form. World No.1 Aryna Sabalenka was knocked out, and apparently told reporters her plan was to 'get completely drunk' after the loss. With Sabalenka gone, the women's draw has opened up significantly, and Osaka — once the world's best — looks primed for a deep run.

stories.title: Aussie juniors Hewitt, Jovanovski and Alame begin strongly at Wimbledon
stories.why_it_matters: Three Australian junior players — Hewitt, Jovanovski and Alame — have all started their Wimbledon campaigns strongly. Tennis Australia flagged the trio as ones to watch as Australia looks to build its next generation of grass-court talent. No specific match details were provided in the article.

stories.title: AFL top-two clubs preview Thursday night blockbuster
stories.why_it_matters: The coaches of the AFL's top two sides have previewed a mouthwatering Thursday night clash this week. The article doesn't name the specific clubs in the available data, but it's shaping up as one of the marquee games of the AFL season so far. Watch for it Thursday night.
